guideTitle: Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens Under $200 (2026)
metaTitle: Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens Under $200 (2026)
metaDescription: Five air fryer toaster ovens at or under $200, led by the Cuisinart 1800W 8-in-1 and Midea Flexify French door, compared on capacity, doors and presets.
expertTake: The Cuisinart 1800W 8-in-1 is the pick at this cap because a 60 minute timer, convection, warm and air fry cover roasting and baking that shorter-timer ovens cannot. The Midea Flexify French door is the value choice for a 26.4 quart interior and ten functions. Anyone who wants a basket-style air fryer's speed should skip toaster ovens and buy a basket unit.
introParagraphs: At the top of the budget range, a toaster oven stops being a toast machine with a fan and starts behaving like a small second oven. Longer timers, larger cavities and better door designs make roasting and baking realistic on the counter.

Prices move, and the $200 cap used here reflects live listing prices when this guide was updated. The extra budget buys timer length, interior size and door design, so the guide separates the upgrades that change cooking from those that only lengthen the preset list.

products.name: Cuisinart 1800W 8-in-1 Air Fryer Toaster Oven with 60 Minute Timer

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Eight, with air fry, convection, broil and warm

products.description:
This Cuisinart is an 1800 watt oven with eight functions, including air fry, convection, broil and warm, and a 60 minute timer. The 0.6 cubic foot interior is large enough to toast six slices of bread or air fry about three pounds of food. A premium build and an upper-end heating system distinguish it from cheaper combos.

The 60 minute timer is the feature that changes what you can cook, because a roast or a casserole often needs more than the 30 minutes that cheaper dials allow. Against the TOA-55 in the lower guide, it adds an eighth function and a longer timer. Next to the Midea Flexify, it is smaller but more powerful, and it uses a conventional drop door.

Preheat for five minutes and use the middle rack. Wipe the stainless with a damp cloth once cool, and empty the crumb tray weekly. Because it pulls 1800W, give it a dedicated outlet and keep it away from a toaster or kettle on the same circuit. The warm function is worth using for dinner parties, since it holds a finished roast at serving temperature for up to an hour without drying it out. A tray of roasted vegetables and a chicken can share the cavity when you place the vegetables on the lower rack and the bird on the upper, which saves a full oven preheat on a busy night.
products.bestFor: Cooks who roast and bake on the counter and need a longer timer.
cons: Larger footprint than a compact combo

products.name: Midea Flexify French Door Toaster Oven Air Fryer Combo, 26.4 Quart

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Ten, including slow cook and dehydrate

products.description:
The Midea Flexify has a 26.4 quart interior with French doors and ten functions: air fry, roast, bake, broil, toast, pizza, reheat, slow cook, dehydrate and warm. A Cyclone air fry system is advertised as 25 percent faster cooking with 90 percent less oil than traditional frying, which are maker claims and depend on the comparison. The French doors open sideways, so the oven needs less depth in front.

The slow cook function is an unusual extra, and it lets the oven hold a stew at low temperature. Set beside the Cuisinart 8-in-1, it has a larger cavity and more functions, but no stated wattage. Measured against the Proctor Silex 4 slice, it is much bigger and needs a lot of counter width.

Measure the counter before ordering, since a 26.4 quart oven is wide. Wipe the door seam after greasy cooks, and empty the crumb tray weekly. Use the rack positions in the manual, and keep the doors closed during cooking to preserve heat. When you use slow cook, start with a recipe designed for a slow cooker and shorten the liquid slightly, since the oven cavity has no sealed lid and more steam escapes than from a crock. A whole chicken fits on the rack with room for vegetables underneath, and the French doors let you baste without a drop-down door in your way.
products.bestFor: Large households that want the biggest cavity and French doors.
cons: Maker claims are comparisons, not measurements

products.name: Hamilton Beach 6 Slice Air Fryer Toaster Oven with Pizza and Reheat

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, toast, pizza, reheat

products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 6 slice carries over from the lower guide as the pick for leftovers. Pizza and reheat functions join the usual air fry, bake, broil and toast, and Sure-Crisp air frying circulates heat around the food. It positions itself as a replacement for a standalone air fryer.

At this cap, it stands out as the simple, familiar choice. Against the Cuisinart 8-in-1, it has fewer functions, no stated wattage and no longer timer, but it costs much less on the price tier. Next to the Proctor Silex 4 slice, it has a larger cavity and more presets.

Use reheat for pizza and fried leftovers, and watch the first few minutes until you learn how it browns. Clean the crumb tray weekly and wipe the walls after cheese drips. Should you plan to roast larger items, the Cuisinart is the better fit. The reheat setting runs at a lower power than a bake setting, which is why a slice of cold pizza ends up with a crisp crust and a hot center instead of a rubbery top. Because the model has no published wattage, judge the preheat by feel on your first two cooks and adjust times accordingly.
products.bestFor: Households that reheat pizza and leftovers and want a familiar brand.
pros: Lower price tier than the Cuisinart
cons: No stated wattage or timer length
Fewer functions than the top picks

products.name: Proctor Silex 4 Slice Air Fryer Toaster Oven, 200 to 450 Degrees
products.description:
The Proctor Silex 4 slice is a compact oven with air fry, bake, broil and toast functions and an adjustable range of 200 to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. Simply-Crisp convection circulates air around food for even browning with little oil. It is the smallest oven in this guide.

Measured against the larger Cuisinart and Midea, it has far less interior and no stated wattage, but it saves counter space and costs less. Set beside the 6 slice Hamilton Beach, it holds fewer items but offers a documented temperature range. It suits a single person or a couple who want one more small appliance.

Place it on a heat-safe surface and give it clearance. Wipe the interior and the crumb tray regularly. If you often cook for more than two, step up to a six-slice model. The 200 degree floor is useful for keeping a dish warm for guests, and a gentle bake at that temperature dries herbs or apple slices if you leave the door cracked. It is a sensible pick for a studio apartment where a full oven is a luxury you rarely heat.
products.bestFor: Singles and couples who want a compact adjustable oven.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 4 Slice Air Fryer Toaster Oven Combo, 30 Minute Timer
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach 4 slice appears here as the simplest option at the lowest price tier in the guide. It offers air fry, bake, broil and toast with a 30 minute timer and a convection fan. The brand is easy to find and the controls are straightforward.

At this cap, the comparison is with the Cuisinart, which offers twice the timer and 1800W. The 4 slice is the pick for someone who wants a small oven for toast and small batches and does not want to pay for more. A 30 minute timer works for most air frying but limits roasts.

Clear the crumb tray weekly and wipe the walls after greasy cooks. Keep the vents clear and use a drip pan under the basket. When you are comparing it with the pricier ovens above, remember that you pay for the timer, the wattage and the cavity, and none of those matter if all you do is crisp frozen snacks and make toast. Many households find that a plain four-slice oven covers ninety percent of their use for a fraction of the cost.
products.bestFor: Small households that want the lowest-cost, simple combo.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 30 minute timer, as on the Hamilton Beach, is fine for air frying but too short for a roast or a casserole. The Cuisinart's 60 minute timer lets you cook a chicken or a lasagna without resetting. Short timers also stop at the end with a ding, and you may need to restart for a longer bake. If you plan to roast, check the maximum timer first. A dial that tops out at 30 minutes forces you to return and reset it, and each reset lets the elements cool and the air in the cavity drop in temperature. Over a two-hour project, that interruption costs you evenness and often lengthens the total cook time.

The Cuisinart offers 0.6 cubic feet, and the Midea offers 26.4 quarts. A 12 inch pizza and a 9 by 13 inch pan are the practical tests. Compact ovens hold a 9 inch pizza and a small pan. Do not buy a bigger oven than your counter can handle, because a unit that blocks the counter will not be used. Check the height under your cabinets as well as the width, and leave at least four inches above the oven for heat to escape. A heat-safe mat under the oven protects stone and laminate counters from the radiant heat of the base.

At 1800W, the Cuisinart preheats quickly and recovers after you open the door. Ovens without a stated wattage often run lower. A weak oven prolongs cook times and dries food. Check the wattage and preheat time when comparing. Many frozen foods are designed around a 425 degree conventional oven, and an oven that takes ten minutes to get there wastes the time you hoped to save. If a listing does not state wattage, assume mid-range heating and plan to add a few minutes to the package instructions.

The Midea's French doors swing aside, while the others drop down. A drop-down door can serve as a shelf, but it blocks the counter in front. French doors need a seal that stays clean. Think about how you load and unload the oven. A heavy casserole is easier to slide in through a wide door opening than a narrow one, and a French door lets you stand square to the oven instead of leaning over a hot drop-down panel. Test the door feel in a store if you can, because hinge stiffness is hard to judge from a photograph.

Air fry, bake, broil, toast and warm cover most tasks. The Midea adds slow cook and dehydrate, and the Hamilton Beach adds pizza and reheat. A function you do not use is just extra clutter on the dial. Look for presets that match what you cook. If you never dehydrate or slow cook, those functions are not a reason to pay more, and if you reheat pizza daily, a good reheat preset is worth more than three extra modes. Write down the three presets you actually use, then check which oven offers them with clear, usable controls.

Grease and cheese bake onto the interior and the elements. Dump the crumb tray weekly and wipe the walls after greasy meals. Exterior surfaces get hot, so leave several inches of clearance and keep the oven off delicate counters. Never leave it unattended while broiling. Fatty foods like bacon and sausage spit and can flare up under the top element, so keep a baking sheet beneath them and check every few minutes. A small kitchen fire extinguisher or a lid for smothering a pan is a sensible companion to any countertop oven.

howWeEvaluated.title: Timer and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared timer length and stated wattage across the lineup. The Cuisinart's 60 minutes and 1800W set the high end, and the Hamilton Beach's 30 minutes set the low end.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Interior volume and footprint were weighed, from the Midea's 26.4 quarts to the Proctor Silex's compact body. Real pan fit counted most.

howWeEvaluated.title: Doors and design
howWeEvaluated.description: The Midea's French doors were compared with drop-down doors on the others. A design that saves counter depth scored for small kitchens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Functions and presets
howWeEvaluated.description: Function sets were weighed, with credit for slow cook and dehydrate on the Midea and for pizza and reheat on the Hamilton Beach.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every item is at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored timer length and heat over a long preset list.

cards.label: Compact (Proctor Silex, Hamilton Beach 4 slice)
cards.text: Small footprint and low price, fine for toast and small batches, but limited for roasts.

cards.label: Large (Midea, Cuisinart)
cards.text: Room for a whole chicken and a 12 inch pizza, but they need counter width and cost more.

howToChoose.note: Pick compact for one or two people, and large for families and roasting.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A timer of at least 60 minutes, convection and an interior that clears the top element. A warm setting holds the meal for guests.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Cuisinart 8-in-1 fits best, with the Midea as the larger option. The 30 minute ovens need resets for long bakes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want to replace a full oven with a countertop one, with a probe, a steam function or a bigger interior. Higher tiers add precise digital controls.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You toast and air fry small batches, in which case a compact oven is enough.

Baked-on grease smokes at the next cook. Use a damp cloth when cool.
Crumbs in the seam let heat escape. Wipe with a damp cloth.
Dials drift by 25 to 50F. A thermometer shows the real heat.
Grease affects flavor. Soak and wash by hand.

faq.q: Can a toaster oven replace a full oven?
faq.a: For small meals, yes. For a large turkey or a sheet pan of cookies, a full oven is still needed.

faq.q: What does the $200 cap buy compared with lower caps?
faq.a: It buys longer timers, bigger interiors and French doors. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: How long do these ovens last?
faq.a: Four to six years with care. The timer, door hinges and heating elements are the likely wear points.

faq.q: Is the slow cook function useful?
faq.a: It works for small batches, and it frees a crock pot. A dedicated slow cooker is still better for large stews.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated outlet?
faq.a: For the 1800W oven, yes. Do not share a circuit with a kettle or microwave.
Yes, in small cut pieces under food. Do not let it touch the elements or the fan.
